title: Aadhaar, PAN, Passport and RTI: Your Rights
summary: When a document is legally required, how to fix errors, report misuse, and use the Right to Information.

body.text: Identity documents prove who you are and unlock services. Knowing when one is legally required, and how to fix problems, protects you from fraud and from being pushed around.

items: Aadhaar: a 12-digit identity number. It is proof of identity, not of citizenship.
PAN: needed for income tax and for many financial transactions above set limits.
Voter ID (EPIC): proves your enrolment as a voter in your constituency.
Passport: proof of identity and citizenship, mainly for travel.
Driving licence: proof that you may drive a particular class of vehicle.

body.text: When a document is legally required, and when it is not

items: Aadhaar is generally required for PAN, many subsidies and KYC, but it is not a universal requirement for every service.
No one can demand your Aadhaar for a service that the law does not link to Aadhaar. Ask for the rule in writing.
A photocopy is usually enough for many private purposes. Do not hand over originals casually.
Corrections to Aadhaar, PAN or the voter roll can be requested through the official portal or office.
If your identity is misused, report it to the police and to the issuing authority.
For financial misuse, call 1930 and report on cybercrime.gov.in the same day.
You can check your Aadhaar authentication history and lock your biometrics online.
Any citizen can ask a public authority for information by filing an RTI application.
The authority must usually reply within 30 days.
If refused or ignored, you can file a first appeal, and then a second appeal to the Information Commission.

body.text: Beware of fake officials and look-alike websites. Genuine government portals use .gov.in or .nic.in. Never pay a 'processing fee' to a personal account or UPI ID.
You can lock your Aadhaar biometrics online so they cannot be used for authentication until you unlock them.
Keep only the copies you need, and never post photos of your Aadhaar, PAN or passport on social media.

practicalSteps: Download or update documents only from official portals such as uidai.gov.in, incometax.gov.in, nvsp.in and passportindia.gov.in.
Use masked Aadhaar (showing only the last 4 digits) wherever it is accepted.
If a document is misused, file a police complaint and an online report the same day.
For a government-service problem, file an RTI or a grievance on the department's portal.
exceptions: Some services are linked to Aadhaar by law; those requirements are lawful even though others are not.
RTI does not cover certain exempt matters, such as national security and personal privacy.

faqs.q: Can a shop or hotel demand my Aadhaar?
faqs.a: Only if the law links that service to Aadhaar. Otherwise you can refuse and offer another accepted ID.

faqs.q: How do I know a government website is real?
faqs.a: Check the domain: official sites use .gov.in or .nic.in and a valid https certificate. Type the address yourself instead of clicking links.

sources.label: Right to Information Act, 2005 - India Code

misconceptions.myth: Aadhaar proves I am an Indian citizen.
misconceptions.fact: Aadhaar is proof of identity, not of citizenship. Citizenship is shown by other documents such as a passport.
